sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Ki? asks who. Mi? asks what. Use Ki ő? to identify a person.

Ki? and Mi? aren’t just two vocabulary words — they’re the seed of a whole word family. Later you’ll meet valaki (‘someone’) and valami (‘something’), and senki (‘no one’) and semmi (‘nothing’), all built by bolting a prefix onto exactly these two roots. Learn ki and mi solidly now and several future words come almost for free.
